title: Dilys's Secret Tunnel
markdown:
Once upon a time, in a garden full of red, yellow, and purple flowers, and herbs that smelled like mint, lived Milo the mole and Fudge the teddy bear. Milo was a busy, kind mole. His nose twitched when he wanted to know things. His very favourite thing was digging wiggly tunnels underground, paths to secret places. Fudge was a cuddly, brave teddy bear, with shiny button eyes and a smile that was always happy. Fudge loved to take long, sunny naps on the softest moss he could find.

Every day was a happy routine. Milo would go digging, exploring the cool earthy world under the dirt. Fudge would find his sunbeam, tuck his paws beneath him, and drift off to sleep. From their garden spot they watched the garden buzz. Butterflies flew like tiny dancers. Birds chirped merry songs from leafy branches. Even the busy ants marched in neat lines, sure they were heading to the big bright lawn for the garden concert.

But as they watched, Milo and Fudge saw a little green beetle named Dilys. Dilys had shiny emerald wings that caught the sunlight. She always stayed by herself, and she looked a little sad.

Every day Dilys sat near the edge of the garden, little legs still. She watched all the other garden friends hop and flutter their way to the music. She really wanted to join them. She wanted to feel the happy tunes moving through her tiny beetle feet. The music drifted over, sweet and inviting. But the big open lawn was so wide. Dilys was a shy beetle. She worried about crossing it all alone. The sun seemed so bright and hot on the wide grass. The tall flowers seemed so far away.

Until one day Dilys could not hold back her wish any longer. Her little heart felt a bit wobbly. She walked slowly to where Milo was peeking out of his tunnel, nose twitching, and Fudge was stretching after a nap, fluffy ears perked up.

“Excuse me,” Dilys whispered. Her little feelers twitched with hope and worry. “I really, really want to hear the concert. But the lawn… it’s so big and wide. I get a little bit worried.” Her voice was so quiet Milo had to wiggle his nose closer and tilt his head to hear.

Milo, with his helpful heart and busy paws, said at once, “Don’t you worry, Dilys. That sounds like a job for a mole. I can dig a secret tunnel right under the lawn. You can travel safely that way. No wide grass to worry about.”

Fudge nodded his fluffy head. His button eyes sparkled. “And I can help too. I can make sure the tunnel is super safe and bright, so you don’t feel lonely in there.”

Because of that, Milo began to dig with all his might. Scratch, scratch, scrabble, went his strong little paws, sending soft earth flying behind him. He dug with a happy rhythm, and made a wonderfully smooth wide path under the green grass, just right for a beetle to run along. Fudge, meanwhile, gathered the tiniest shiniest dewdrops he could find, and put them carefully along the tunnel walls. They shone like little stars and made a soft gentle light. He also pushed away any little stones that might be in the way, and made sure the leafy bits that fell in were soft and cosy, like a little carpet.

Dilys watched from her spot. Her heart felt a little lighter with every scoop Milo made. She felt cared for by every dewdrop Fudge placed.

When the tunnel was finished, smelling fresh and earthy, Milo nudged Dilys gently with his soft nose. “It’s ready, Dilys. Just a little way down, and then you’ll pop up right near the concert. It’s perfectly safe.”

Until finally Dilys took a deep breath. Her little lungs filled with the nice smell of the soil. The tunnel was not dark, not really. She could see the soft glow of the dewdrops Fudge had placed, twinkling like little guides. Drip, drip, drip went the dewdrops, a gentle peaceful sound. Milo’s soft digging, far away, was a nice hum, like a sleepy song. She could smell the sweet damp earth all around her. She took her first brave step and scurried along the smooth tunnel.

At last Dilys’s little feelers popped out from under a soft velvety bit of a bright pink flower. She had arrived, right there on the very edge of the concert lawn, hidden among the pretty flowers. The music was even more beautiful up close, a lively tune played on tiny flutes and humming bees. A soft sweet breeze tickled her wings and carried the lovely smell of flowers from a nearby bush. She saw Milo and Fudge sitting on a smooth grey stone at the edge of the lawn, giving her a happy wave. Dilys took another deep breath. Her worry went away like morning mist. She wiggled her feet and hopped onto a soft velvety daisy, and felt the merry rhythm from her feelers to her tiny toes.

Ever since then, Dilys the beetle never missed a single garden concert. She always used Milo and Fudge’s special secret tunnel. After the last tune, when the lawn grew quiet, she would wander back the earthy way, past the little star-dewdrops, and settle near the moss where Fudge napped, wings folded, the music still humming softly in her feet as she drifted toward sleep, knowing she had such kind friends, and a tunnel that would be there in the morning.
